title: Consolidate Console API aggregators, stabilize GraphQL resolvers, and normalize caching layers
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The Console backend has accrued multiple overlapping aggregation layers between REST endpoints and the GraphQL shim. This manifests as duplicated data fetches, inconsistent cache TTLs, and several p95 tail latency spikes on routes that aggregate model, billing, and usage metadata.

Goal: Reduce end-to-end Console API p95 latency by 25-35% for aggregation-heavy routes, reduce redundant DB/remote calls, and standardize caching semantics so dashboards and rollout pages see consistent, fresher data. Deliverables: 1) Single aggregation layer library for Console that both REST handlers and GraphQL resolvers import. 2) Replace ad-hoc caches with a small, observable LRU cache wrapper that emits hit/miss metrics and supports per-key TTLs and invalidation hooks. 3) Refactor GraphQL resolvers to use batched data loaders where appropriate and avoid N+1. 4) Add request-level trace IDs for internal routing and ensure aggregation calls are cancellable on client disconnect.

Scope: Surface routes: /console/projects/:id/overview, /console/rollouts/:id, and /console/usage/* as first wave. Backend areas touched: aggregation service (services/aggregator), GraphQL resolvers (graphql/resolvers/*), REST handlers (api/handlers/*), shared cache util (lib/cache), and telemetry (metrics/collector).

Non-goals: This ticket does not change persistence schemas or perform DB partitioning. It also does not address Dedicated runtime performance outside Console API surface.

Success metrics: - p95 latency reduction of 25%+ on targeted routes (measured from CDN edge to backend) - at least 2x cache hit ratio improvement on aggregated keys - 10-20% reduction in CPU time spent by aggregation flows in staging perf tests - no increase in error rate or cache inconsistency incidents post-rollout

Rollout plan: feature-flagged in staging, small canary in production for 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor dashboards, then gradual ramp to 100% with quick rollback flag.

Testing: unit tests for aggregator library, integration tests mocking upstream model/usage services, end-to-end load test in perf environment (target QPS with representative token sizes), and manual smoke tests for observed pages.

Notes: See design doc and perf dashboard links below for benchmarks and data shapes.
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Chen: Created ticket after spike analysis showed duplicated fetches between /overview route and GraphQL endpoint. Linked initial perf snapshot: https://dashboard.internal.redwood/console/perf/snapshots/2025-02-10

2025-02-14 Rohan Patel: Did initial code walkthrough. Found three separate aggregation helpers: services/aggregator/v1, api/utils/aggregateRecent, graphql/helpers/aggregate. Proposing a single minimal API: aggregate(keys[], context, opts) -> {data, stale}

2025-02-17 Engineering Sync: Agreed to standardize on Promise-based cancelable calls. Infra noted we must ensure no long-lived context prevents GC (infra@callout). Added ENG-8055 as follow-up to add request-scoped cancel tokens across the stack.

2025-02-20 Design Review (Ava Martinez): Confirmed UX can tolerate 2s TTL on billing summaries; product prefers fresher data for rollouts (TTL 30s). Adjusted caching policy table in design doc: https://confluence.redwood/console/agg-cache-policies

2025-02-24 Rohan Patel: Implemented lib/cache LRU wrapper with Prometheus metrics (cache_hits_total, cache_misses_total, cache_evictions_total). Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4121

2025-02-26 Maya Chen: Performance run in perf env: overview p95 dropped from 520ms -> 360ms (31% improvement) after removing duplicate model metadata fetch; cache hit ratio 0.62 -> 0.78. Noted higher variance on rollout page due to large multi-entity joins.

2025-02-28 QA: Found an edge case where GraphQL resolver batched loader returned partial results when one upstream timed out, causing inconsistent UI cards. Added retry-with-backoff for tolerant keys and fail-open for non-critical keys. See notes in PR review.

2025-03-02 Security: Requested a short review for the cache invalidation API to ensure no sensitive tokens are stored in memory. Response: ok if we scrub keys and rely on KMS for encrypted values. Added cleaning step to cache key gen.

2025-03-03 Rohan Patel: Merged aggregator consolidation PR to staging (PR 4121). Preparing canary flag and smoke test checklist. Follow-ups: add end-to-end tracing (ENG-8270), and increase integration test coverage for partial failures (ENG-8289).
acceptance_criteria: All targeted routes use the new aggregator library and no longer call legacy aggregation helpers
Cache wrapper emits metrics and is configured with TTLs per key type
GraphQL resolvers rely on batch loaders and avoid N+1 for the identified queries
Perf tests in staging show >=25% p95 improvement for overview and >=10% for rollout pages, with no regression in error rates
Feature flag present for instant rollback and canary control
